_comment: Per-skill install catalog for the /jarvis-setup page. One entry per skill the plugin can install individually (replaces the old core/research/media category toggles). Every license/author claim here was checked against a primary source (a local LICENSE file, or upstream raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<branch>/LICENSE) -- never a README claim or blog post. See setup/server.mjs's report-back for the exact sources read. `id` must match the skill's directory name under skills/ (or optional-skills/ when disabled). Entries that carry an `install` array (animation bundle, Modern Web Guidance) are RECOMMENDED EXTERNAL installs: no directory under skills/ or optional-skills/, no toggle on the page, only copyable upstream install commands. Their license was read from the upstream LICENSE file unless the entry's `note` says otherwise. Their `id` therefore does not map to a directory.

skills.name: Shufi Design (main design skill)
skills.description: Designs a site or screen as live directions you pick from
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.note: Original to this project. This is the process Shufi's own setup page was designed with; Shufi custom.
skills.details: The design process Shufi was built with: references first, 6 live clickable directions in one tabbed page, then narrowed by your words. Shufi custom.

skills.name: Modern Web Guidance (Google Chrome)
skills.description: Keeps generated web code on current browser features and best practices
skills.author: Google Chrome
skills.note: Recommended external install, not bundled. Apache-2.0 read from the upstream LICENSE file. The marketplace is named googlechrome.
skills.details: Searchable guides from the Chrome team so the code Claude writes uses modern CSS, HTML and web APIs instead of stale patterns. Run it alongside the design skill.

skills.name: GSAP skills (official)
skills.description: Scroll animation, timelines and SVG: the default for page motion
skills.author: GreenSock
skills.details: Official GreenSock skills: core API, timelines, ScrollTrigger, plugins, React and framework use. Pick this first for anything on a page or tied to scroll.

skills.name: Motion (official)
skills.description: Micro-interactions, springs and gestures in React and Vue
skills.author: Motion
skills.note: The MIT grant is the license field of the npm package motion-ai; the repository has no LICENSE file, so it is recommended here and never vendored. Docs search and audits use Motion's hosted MCP, which the installer offers.
skills.details: Official Motion (formerly Framer Motion) skill: best practices for Motion and CSS, spring generator, performance audit. Pick it when the project is already React or Vue.

skills.name: Motion design principles (LottieFiles)
skills.description: Timing, easing and choreography rules before you animate
skills.author: LottieFiles
skills.details: Tool-agnostic motion design principles (not a Lottie generator): decide what the motion should feel like, then build it with GSAP, Motion or CSS.

skills.name: Rive (official)
skills.description: Interactive animation that reacts to the user, built from text
skills.author: Rive
skills.details: Official Rive skill: agents build interactive Rive files with the Rive CLI. Heavier than GSAP; pick it when the animation must respond to input and run on web and mobile.

skills.name: Three.js skills
skills.description: 3D scenes, shaders and glTF animation on the web
skills.author: CloudAI-X
skills.note: Third-party, not published by the three.js project (it ships no skill of its own).
skills.details: Thirteen three.js skills (scene, materials, shaders, animation, React Three Fiber). Use only for real 3D; for 2D parallax use GSAP.

skills.name: Impeccable animate pass
skills.description: Polishes motion on an interface that already exists
skills.author: Paul Bakaus
skills.note: The closest upstream match for the UI-animation item in the animation skill roundup; that page links no repository.
skills.details: The animate command inside Impeccable: reviews and refines the motion of a finished interface. Run it after the design skill, not instead of it.

skills.name: Session Wrap-Up (done)
skills.description: Saves what happened, so nothing is lost
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Writes a session note, folds it into hub memory, and commits the hub -- run this at the end of every session.

skills.name: Setup For Me
skills.description: Claude does the setup itself; you only do keys and sign-ins
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Runs every step of the setup page from the terminal, asks once before installing software, and hands back only what needs a person.

skills.name: Memory Consolidation
skills.description: Turns recent sessions into lasting memory
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Folds recent session logs into the hub's memory files so patterns and decisions persist.

skills.name: Wiki Article
skills.description: Keeps what you figured out as a short note
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Turns a discovery or research session into a short reference article instead of losing it to scrollback.

skills.name: Grill Me
skills.description: Questions your plan until it holds up
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Interviews you about a plan or design until every branch of the decision actually holds together.

skills.name: Learn
skills.description: Keeps takeaways from books and courses
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Captures book, course, or article takeaways into a structured, dated personal learning log.

skills.name: ELI5 Visual Explainer
skills.description: Explains with pictures instead of walls of text
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.note: The instructions are original, not copied from a licensed repo -- no matching skill exists in kepano/obsidian-skills or anthropics/skills (both checked). The file itself credits the underlying prompting pattern to Thariq (Anthropic) via a public tweet and https://leslieli.dev/notes/anthropic-eli5-skill-html-artifacts/ -- that's an idea credit, not a license grant, since no redistributable source file was found to vendor from.
skills.details: Explains a concept or codebase as a visual, big-picture HTML artifact instead of a wall of text.

skills.name: Defuddle
skills.description: Turns a web page into clean, readable text
skills.author: Steph Ango (@kepano)
skills.note: Vendored byte-identical to upstream (diff against raw.githubusercontent.com/kepano/obsidian-skills/main/skills/defuddle/SKILL.md is empty).
skills.details: Strips a web page down to clean markdown locally, before you read or summarize it.

skills.name: QMD
skills.description: Searches everything you have written
skills.author: Tobi Lutke
skills.note: Bundled copy is a hand-trimmed fork of upstream v2.0.0; current upstream is v2.2.0 and has since added --full-path, line-slicing, and `qmd doctor` that this copy doesn't have.
skills.details: Local hybrid search (keyword + embeddings) over your own markdown notes.

skills.name: Research Notebook
skills.description: Researches a topic and cites its sources
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.note: Needs the separate `notebooklm` CLI installed and authenticated with a Google account -- not bundled, no API key involved.
skills.details: Drives NotebookLM to ingest sources, ask questions, and return a cited research synthesis.

skills.name: Media Gen
skills.description: Makes images and video from a description
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Photoreal image and video generation and upscaling via fal.ai, pay-per-use.

skills.name: Playwright CLI
skills.description: Checks a website and takes screenshots
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.note: Bundles the `playwright` npm package; first run downloads real browser binaries (tens of MB), which is why this defaults off rather than because of any license concern.
skills.requires_tool: Node.js (already required) + Playwright browser binaries, downloaded on first run
skills.details: Disk-based Playwright QA scan for a running site -- screenshots, console errors, and broken-link checks in one report.

skills.name: Obsidian CLI
skills.description: Reads and writes notes in Obsidian
skills.author: Steph Ango (@kepano)
skills.note: Vendored byte-identical to upstream (diff against raw.githubusercontent.com/kepano/obsidian-skills/main/skills/obsidian-cli/SKILL.md is empty). Needs Obsidian actually running, not just installed, to do anything -- same detect precondition as the other three, no stronger check implemented for the running-vs-installed distinction.
skills.details: Reads, creates, and searches notes in a running Obsidian instance from the command line.

skills.name: Obsidian Markdown
skills.description: Writes notes the way Obsidian expects
skills.author: Steph Ango (@kepano)
skills.note: Vendored byte-identical to upstream (diff against raw.githubusercontent.com/kepano/obsidian-skills/main/skills/obsidian-markdown/SKILL.md is empty).
skills.details: Writes valid Obsidian-flavored markdown -- wikilinks, embeds, callouts, and frontmatter properties.

skills.name: Obsidian Bases
skills.description: Builds live tables from your notes
skills.author: Steph Ango (@kepano)
skills.note: Near-identical to upstream (497 vs 499 lines) -- a couple of filter-example lines differ (simplified vs. upstream's fuller example), same tool and scope.
skills.details: Creates and edits Obsidian .base files -- database-like table/card/list views over your notes.

skills.name: JSON Canvas
skills.description: Builds mind maps and flowcharts as notes
skills.author: Steph Ango (@kepano)
skills.note: Vendored byte-identical to upstream (diff against raw.githubusercontent.com/kepano/obsidian-skills/main/skills/json-canvas/SKILL.md is empty).
skills.details: Creates and edits .canvas files -- nodes, edges, and groups for mind maps and flowcharts in Obsidian.

skills.name: Voice
skills.description: Talk to it, and hear it answer
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Speech in and speech out. Transcribes voice notes with ElevenLabs Scribe and falls back to whisper running locally on your own machine; speaks replies with ElevenLabs text-to-speech. Without a key the transcription half still works offline.

skills.name: Council
skills.description: Pressure-tests a big decision from several angles
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Five independent advisors, an anonymous peer review and a chair's verdict -- for real forks in the road, not small calls.

skills.name: Knowledge Pack
skills.description: Builds a lasting reference on one subject
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: A short always-read index plus numbered files, every claim sourced and graded, researched in parallel.

skills.name: Preflight
skills.description: Checks env files and paths before you deploy
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Catches quoting mistakes in env files, non-ASCII paths with Next.js and swallowed errors before a production deploy.

skills.name: Release Watch
skills.description: Tells you only what is new and relevant in Claude Code
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: Reads the Claude Code changelog, keeps what matters for your setup, writes a dated digest to the hub. Silence is a valid result.

skills.name: Session Recall (experimental)
skills.description: Finds what you decided in earlier sessions
skills.author: jarvis-os project
skills.details: EXPERIMENTAL and opt-in. After enabling it with a flag file in your hub, each session of 5+ messages makes one `claude -p` call (uses your subscription usage) to write a short note into the hub's staging/ folder only, never the hub itself; a start-of-session index lists recent sessions. Needs a valid `claude` login; session-end capture is not verified when closing a Claude Desktop window.
